make.name: GAC Aion
make.description: GAC Group's electric-car company, founded in 2017 as GAC New Energy. It sells the mass-market Aion range in China and, under the GAC name, in Southeast Asia, Europe and Australia; its premium brand Hyptec is listed separately.

models.name: Aion S
models.description: Aion's first car, a compact executive sedan on sale in China since May 2019. Rebadged versions were sold as the GAC-Toyota iA5 and GAC-Honda EA6.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 58.8 kWh CATL NMC pack and a front motor of about 180 hp.

models.name: Aion S Plus
models.description: Restyled, larger successor-in-spirit to the Aion S launched in 2021 alongside it; exported as the Aion ES.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 204 hp front motor with LFP or NMC packs up to 69.9 kWh (510-610 km CLTC).

models.name: Aion S Max
models.description: Larger, more powerful version of the S family launched in 2023 and dropped in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 180 kW front motor; LFP packs of 59.5-67.9 kWh (510-610 km CLTC).

models.name: Aion RT
models.description: Mid-size sedan on the AEP 3.0 platform launched in China in 2024 with CATL packs; a battery-swap RT Super followed in April 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 55.1 or 68.1 kWh CATL LFP packs; RT Super uses a swappable 54 kWh Choco-SEB pack.

models.name: Aion UT
models.description: Compact electric hatchback launched in China in February 2025 (Yingwulong, 'parrot dragon') and exported to Europe, Australia and Southeast Asia. Sold in Russia as the UMO 3.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 100 kW front motor in China; export models use a 60 kWh pack and 150 kW.

models.name: Aion V
models.description: Compact SUV. The first generation (2020-2024) was refreshed as the V Plus in 2021; the second generation (2024, 'Tyrannosaurus Rex' in China) is GAC's global model, sold in Europe from September 2025 and Australia from November 2025.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 135 kW front motor, CATL packs, V 60/70/80 trims.

generations.name: V Plus
generations.description: Restyled V Plus with 70-95 kWh packs and fast-charging battery option.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: All-new AEP 3.0 SUV with 62, 75 or 90 kWh packs.

models.name: Aion i60
models.description: 2025 derivative of the second-generation Aion V offered with range-extender and battery-electric powertrains.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: BEV with a 150 or 165 kW front motor.

models.name: Aion Y
models.description: Tall compact crossover launched in 2021, refreshed and lengthened as the Aion Y Plus in October 2022 and widely exported in Southeast Asia. Replaced in China by the Aion N60 in 2026. Sold in Russia as the UMO 5.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Original Aion Y with 135 kW front motor.

generations.name: Y Plus
generations.description: Longer Y Plus with 150 kW motor and 64 kWh LFP or 76.8 kWh NMC pack.

models.name: Aion LX
models.description: Mid-size SUV launched in 2019, Aion's second car; the restyled LX Plus (2021) offered a 144 kWh pack. Production ended in 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 70 or 93 kWh CATL NMC packs, FWD or 300 kW AWD.

generations.name: LX Plus
generations.description: Restyled LX Plus with up to 144.4 kWh NMC pack.

models.name: Aion N60
models.description: Compact SUV launched in April 2026 as the Chinese-market successor to the Aion Y, with WeRide driver assistance and LiDAR as standard.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 165 kW front motor, three LFP pack sizes.
